codemap:
The issue changes prose only: the pages that tell whoever edits this repository how to write a rule, the frontmatter descriptions those rules are then applied to, and the repository's own suite that guards them.

What INC-1's attempt established, and what INC-3 works from: the two existing authoring pages are each scoped to one audience, so neither could house a rule binding both, and the shipped brief was rejected as a home because it ships to every project and binds agents at run time rather than the people who write uroboros pages. The attempt's files are on the unmerged remote branch `claude/authoring-rule-form-matching-c5ygkt--INC-1`.

The home of the new rules:

- `.claude/rules/authoring.md` — new page, path-scoped to `skills/**` and `agents/**`, the one home for the four-row failure-to-form table, the exemption-clause ban and (in INC-2) the description rule. Created by INC-1's attempt; INC-3 lands it again on the issue branch.
- `skills/CLAUDE.md` — the authoring rules for skill pages; carries a one-sentence pointer to the new page and nothing that restates it. Its "What a page has to carry" states what a skill `description` is for, so the INC-2 description rule lands on or against that text.
- `.claude/rules/agents.md` — the authoring rules for agent pages, path-scoped to `agents/**`; carries the same one-sentence pointer. Its "What a page has to carry" states what an agent `description` is for.

The suite:

- `test-repo.sh` — the suite that owns facts about the repository itself and the only home for a mechanical check over these pages; already listed in `test.sh`, so no new entry is needed there. It is where the guards for the table rows, the exemption ban and (in INC-2) the description rule live, and where INC-1 failed: three of its four row checks matched a whole table line rather than the cell naming the form that works.

The descriptions INC-2's rule is applied to:

- `skills/agent-brief/SKILL.md` — shipped skill description, checked and rewritten if it summarises steps.
- `skills/argus/SKILL.md` — same.
- `skills/grill/SKILL.md` — same.
- `skills/retro/SKILL.md` — same.
- `agents/planner.md` — agent description, checked against the rule and rewritten only where it contradicts the body of its own page.
- `agents/researcher.md` — same.
- `agents/implementer.md` — same.
- `agents/reviewer.md` — same.
- `agents/test-author.md` — same.

Checked and out of scope: `rulebook.md` and `GEMINI.md` steer the session's own conduct and carry no rules about writing a page's frontmatter or a rule's form; `README.md` paraphrases the skills but copies no frontmatter description verbatim; the suite docs under `hooks/`, `tools/*/` and `skills/agent-brief/assets/` document test suites, not authoring; `test.sh` needs no change because it already runs `test-repo.sh`.

increments.title: The authoring rules pick a rule's form by the failure it prevents
increments.goal: Whoever edits a page in this repository finds in the authoring rules a four-row table that picks the form of a correction from the failure class it prevents, and a standing ban on patching a working rule with an exemption clause. Today that choice is made by taste and re-learned through failed agent runs.
criteria: The authoring rules carry a table of exactly four rows; each row names a failure class, the form that works against it, the form that fails against it, and the reason in one sentence.

The four rows are: a rule skipped under pressure gets a prohibition carrying its price and the verbatim rationalisation it counters; a wrong output shape gets a recipe stating what the output is; an omitted required element gets a required slot in the schema or template; behaviour that depends on a condition gets a rule keyed to an observable predicate.
The authoring rules forbid patching an existing rule with an exemption clause and require re-cutting the rule on an observable predicate instead.

The table and the exemption rule reach whoever authors a skill page and whoever authors an agent page alike, and the repository's existing rule about one home per rule is not broken to achieve it — no page restates what another page already carries.
The commands the increment names all exit 0.
increments.note: The review rejected this attempt after two correction rounds: the four-row table and the exemption-clause ban were written correctly, but the suite guarded three of the four rows so loosely that a table pairing a failure class with the form that loses against it would still pass. The attempt's work is on the remote branch claude/authoring-rule-form-matching-c5ygkt--INC-1, which was not merged and stays off the issue branch; INC-3 re-cuts the same delivery with the guard bar written into its criteria.

increments.title: The form table lands, and every row of it is guarded against its own inversion
increments.goal: Whoever edits a page in this repository finds in the authoring rules a four-row table that picks the form of a correction from the failure class it prevents, and a standing ban on patching a working rule with an exemption clause — and the repository's own suite holds each of those four rows to the form that wins, so the table cannot silently drift into pairing a failure class with the form that loses against it. This re-cuts INC-1, whose prose satisfied every criterion but whose guards did not; the prior attempt is on the unmerged remote branch claude/authoring-rule-form-matching-c5ygkt--INC-1 and can be read there.
criteria: The authoring rules carry a table of exactly four rows; each row names a failure class, the form that works against it, the form that fails against it, and the reason in one sentence.

The four rows are: a rule skipped under pressure gets a prohibition carrying its price and the verbatim rationalisation it counters; a wrong output shape gets a recipe stating what the output is; an omitted required element gets a required slot in the schema or template; behaviour that depends on a condition gets a rule keyed to an observable predicate.
The authoring rules forbid patching an existing rule with an exemption clause and require re-cutting the rule on an observable predicate instead.

The table and the exemption rule reach whoever authors a skill page and whoever authors an agent page alike, and the repository's existing rule about one home per rule is not broken to achieve it — no page restates what another page already carries.

For each of the four rows independently, a table that pairs that row's failure class with the form that fails against it instead of the form that works turns the suite red; a check that would still pass on such a table does not satisfy this criterion.
Deleting the price, deleting the verbatim rationalisation, deleting the exemption-clause ban, or dropping the observable predicate from the re-cutting requirement each turns the suite red.
The commands the increment names all exit 0.
increments.note: INC-1 blocked on exactly the fifth criterion above; the sixth records what the earlier correction rounds already fixed, so it is not lost when the work is done again.

increments.title: A description names the occasion, and every shipped description is held to it
increments.goal: The authoring rules state what a description is for — the occasion to reach for the thing, never its steps — and every description this repository ships is checked against that rule, so no description can be read as a shortcut past the body it fronts.
criteria: The authoring rules require a description to name the occasion for using the thing and forbid it from summarising the thing's steps, with the reason a summarised workflow becomes a shortcut agents take instead of reading the body.

Each of the four shipped skill descriptions — `agent-brief`, `argus`, `grill`, `retro` — is checked against that rule, and each one that summarises steps is rewritten so it names the occasion instead.
A rewritten skill description still leads with the words a request for that skill would actually contain, so discovery still finds it.

Each of the five agent descriptions is checked against that rule, and rewritten only where the description contradicts the body of the page it fronts; a description that merely summarises steps without contradicting its page is left as it stands.
The increment's return records the verdict for all nine descriptions by name, including the ones deliberately left unchanged and why.
The commands the increment names all exit 0.

steps.label: decompose

return.summary: Cut the issue into two increments: INC-1 puts the four-row form table and the ban on exemption-clause patches into the authoring rules, INC-2 adds the rule that a description names the occasion and applies it to all four shipped skill descriptions and all five agent descriptions. The codemap names the two authoring pages (skills/CLAUDE.md, .claude/rules/agents.md), the nine description-bearing pages and test-repo.sh.
